viewsWelcome.resourceTree:
The Custom Resource Tree only organizes folders; it never moves or deletes files on disk.
[New Virtual Group](command:wispkit.resourceTree.addGroup)
[Add Folder](command:wispkit.resourceTree.addFolder)

The tree is stored in `.WispkitView/resource-tree.json` in the workspace. You can export and import it; after editing it externally, click Refresh in the view title bar to reload.

config.toc.enabled.description: Show the table of contents sidebar in the Wispkit Markdown view.
config.toc.depth.description: Deepest heading level listed in the table of contents. Markdown supports six heading levels (h1–h6); the default lists all of them.
config.zoom.wheelStep.description: Zoom factor applied per wheel notch.
config.image.wheelZoom.description: Zoom the image on a plain wheel scroll, without holding Ctrl.
config.image.dragButton.description: Mouse button that pans the image while held down.
config.xaml.codeVisible.description: Show the source pane on the left side of the XAML view (side by side with the rendered output).
config.xaml.codeWidth.description: Width of the source pane on the left side of the XAML view, in pixels.
config.readonly.default.description: Whether to enter global read-only mode on startup (you can also toggle it from the status bar at any time).
config.readonly.previewBytes.description: Maximum number of bytes loaded in read-only mode; anything beyond this is not loaded (to save rendering cost).
config.readonly.previewLines.description: Maximum number of lines shown in read-only mode.
config.readonly.extensions.description: File glob patterns that global read-only mode applies to (written into workbench.editorAssociations so these files open in the read-only view by default). Deliberately excludes the browsing types Wispkit handles itself (.md/.html/.xaml/images) — truncating them would render incomplete results.
config.subtree.columns.description: Columns shown in the subtree view (array order is column order).
config.subtree.tools.description: Custom tools on the right side of the subtree view; command/args can use ${file} ${dir} ${name} ${workspaceFolder}.
config.subtree.typeAhead.description: Type-ahead in the subtree list, the way Explorer does it: typing a letter or a digit jumps to the first entry starting with it, and pressing the same character again moves further down. Chinese names match whatever the input method commits. The comparison runs over the visible rows only.
config.resourceTree.file.description: Location of the custom resource tree JSON file. Relative paths are based on the first workspace folder; supports the ${workspaceFolder} placeholder and absolute paths.
config.shellLink.openBehavior.descriptio: Default response for .lnk files: system = hand it to Windows (same as double-clicking in Explorer), internal = open the target inside Wispkit, ask = ask every time.
config.shellLink.folderTarget.descriptio: Where to land when opening internally and the target is a folder: subtree = jump inside the subtree panel, system = hand it to the system file manager.
config.shellLink.allowEdit.description: Allow rewriting the target path, working directory, arguments and description directly from the .lnk property page (Windows only).
config.executable.openBehavior.descripti: Default response for .exe files: system = let Windows run it, viewer = open the Wispkit PE property page, ask = ask every time.
